bull.b: The long-duration Rockdale lease shifts part of Riot’s model toward contracted data-center infrastructure revenue. Its large capacity, long initial term, and projected high NOI margin could improve revenue visibility as phased construction is completed.

AMD expansion and a growing engineering backlog support diversification beyond self-mining. Vertical integration, increased manufacturing capacity, and improved engineering margins may help Riot control delivery risks and capture more data-center value.

Large deployed hash rate and favorable power economics can strengthen Riot’s position in a competitive mining industry. Lower energy costs support mining resilience and provide operating scale, although returns remain dependent on network conditions.

bear.t: Deep Losses and Weak Cash Generation
bear.b: Persistent losses and cash consumption weaken internal funding capacity and reduce capital efficiency. With deeply negative ROE and recurring negative free cash flow, Riot may need sustained execution improvements before its expansion can become self-funded.

bear.t: High Capital Intensity and Funding Dependence
bear.b: Riot’s data-center strategy requires substantial construction spending before full revenue realization. Dependence on project debt, asset sales, and possible equity funding creates execution and refinancing risk across the multi-year buildout.

Self-mining remains exposed to bitcoin prices, rising network competition, and operating downtime. These factors can compress mining revenue and margins even when Riot expands hash rate, leaving earnings structurally volatile during the transition.
